title: Empty results must declare themselves empty: absence of evidence keeps rendering as evidence of absence
description:
A repo-wide contract ticket, not a single-site bug. Minted 2026-08-02 after the same defect class was confirmed THREE times in one day, in three unrelated subsystems. Two instances have been fixed at their individual call sites; nothing prevents the fourth.

**The class.** A operation produces an empty result — zero items selected, zero installed, an empty set of things to check — and reports success. The caller cannot distinguish "nothing needed doing" from "the thing that finds work is broken and found nothing." Absence of evidence is rendered as evidence of absence.

**Confirmed instances (all three verified this week, not hypothetical):**

1. **`test:since` zero-spec selection.** A ref that fails to resolve, or a diff range that selects nothing, produces "No test files found" — visually indistinguishable from a green run. `CLAUDE.md` already warns in PROSE that "a zero-specs result from `test:since` is a gate FAILURE to investigate, never a green" — which is exactly the shape of control this repo has repeatedly found insufficient. The warning is real; the enforcement is a human remembering to read it.

2. **`reconcile-apply` returning `installed: []` with `ok: true`.** Every built-in pack skill soft-failed to materialize, nothing installed, and the CLI reported unqualified success. This shipped through at least two releases and broke `/hivemind:design-pack`'s headline promise for every downstream consumer. Fixed at that call site by TASK-181 (adding counts) and TASK-183 (adding a failure predicate and a non-zero exit).

3. **The design-pack doc-lock's empty checked-set.** The spec derived the field names it would verify from a SUCCESS-path fixture run. Failure-only fields (`code`, `message`) therefore formed an empty set — which was dutifully checked, passed, and reported green while the document it guarded was materially wrong. The lock had been written that same morning specifically to prevent silent drift. Fixed at that site by TASK-184.

Three subsystems, one root shape. Instances 2 and 3 were each fixed in isolation, by different tickets, without either recognizing the other as the same defect.

**The contract to establish (this is the deliverable).** An operation that can return an empty result must make emptiness self-describing: the result carries enough information for a caller to tell "zero because there was nothing to do" apart from "zero because the search/selection/derivation failed." The `planned_install_count` / `installed_count` pair TASK-183 added is the reference implementation — zero installed is fine when zero were planned, and a hard failure when two were.

**IMPORTANT — do not over-apply this.** "Empty responses are always false" is too strong and would produce a wave of false positives. Plenty of empty results are legitimate and unambiguous (`list_todos` on a drained board; a diff that genuinely touches nothing). The rule is NOT "reject empty"; it is **"empty must be distinguishable from failed, and the caller must never have to infer which."** A seam where emptiness is already unambiguous needs no change, and saying so explicitly is a valid outcome for that seam.

**Scope guidance.** The audit is the valuable part — the fixes are mostly small once a seam is identified. Prioritise seams where an empty result feeds a GATE or a decision (test selection, guard evaluation, sensor derivation, install/apply counts), over seams where it merely feeds a display.
acceptance_criteria: An audit enumerates the seams in this repo where an operation can return an empty/zero result that a caller could read as success. The enumeration is recorded (a doc or the closing comment) with, for each seam, whether emptiness is currently self-describing or ambiguous. Prioritise seams feeding a gate, guard, sensor, or count over display-only seams. An honest 'this seam is already unambiguous' is a valid per-seam outcome.

The contract is written down in a durable location (CLAUDE.md's Testing/Rules section or a docs/ page, whichever fits the existing structure) in the form: an operation that can return empty must let the caller distinguish 'nothing to do' from 'the finder failed', and MUST NOT report unqualified success for the latter. Cite the three confirmed instances as the motivating evidence so a future reader can see the class, not just the rule.

The two already-fixed instances are verified to CONFORM to the written contract rather than merely being patched — reconcile-apply's planned/installed counts and the doc-lock's failure-path derivation. If either fix does not actually satisfy the contract as written, say so and reconcile the two.

The test:since zero-spec case is closed mechanically rather than by prose: scripts/test-since.mjs (or its caller) fails loudly, with a non-zero exit, when a resolved ref selects zero specs — or, if that turns out to produce false failures in a legitimate case (a genuinely empty diff), the seam is made unambiguous some other way and the reasoning is recorded. Verify against a real zero-selection run, not a mocked one.

At least one new seam beyond the three known instances is either fixed or explicitly cleared. If the audit genuinely finds none, state that and show the search that supports it — a null result here is acceptable ONLY if it is itself self-describing, which is the point of the ticket.

ESCALATION CLAUSE: if any seam identified turns out to sit on a close-guard, state-mutation, or security path, do NOT fix it here — surface it and it will be minted as its own tdd ticket. This ticket is tests-after because the expected work is additive assertions and reporting; a guard-path change is not.
npm run test:all is green; no existing spec regresses; if any bundled source changed, dist rebuilt via npm run build:plugin and committed with tests/e2e/dist-parity.spec.js passing.

comments.author: orchestrator
comments.body:
CLOSED on a green review. **APPROVE — 0 HIGH / 2 MEDIUM / 3 LOW.** All 7 ACs PASS. Review depth `full` (mandatory-FULL surface: test infrastructure — `scripts/test-since.mjs` is the wrapper the Reviewer gate itself runs on every ticket).

## AC1 — THE FULL SEAM ENUMERATION (recorded here because the AC requires durability, and losing it would be this ticket's own defect class applied to itself)

Ten seams audited. One fixed, two verified conforming, six cleared as already unambiguous, one escalated.

| Seam | Disposition |
|---|---|
| `test:since` zero-spec selection | **FIXED** — AC4, self-describing markers, non-fatal |
| `reconcile-apply` `installed: []` + `ok:true` (`bin/pack-ctl.js:461-490, 522-528`) | **VERIFIED CONFORMING** (TASK-181/183). `planned_install_count`/`installed_count` always present; `ok` requires full success and no abort; `ok:false` exits 1 with `code`+`message` on stderr. Not touched — already correct. |
| Design-pack doc-lock's success-path-only checked set (`tests/e2e/design-pack-doc-lock.spec.js`) | **VERIFIED CONFORMING** (TASK-184). Now derives checked fields from a real failure-path run too; word-boundary predicate replaces the substring match. Not touched. |
| `scripts/verify-manifests.mjs`'s `hasAny` empty-manifest check | **CLEARED — already unambiguous.** Prints an explicit "no implementation/manifests found — nothing to verify" before exit 0, distinct from the FAIL branch which is only reachable once checks actually execute. Spot-checked independently by the reviewer at `:30-35`. |
| `src/graph-freshness.js#findDoneTicketsMissingGraphNodes` returning `[]` | **CLEARED** — deterministic from validated inputs; upstream load failures throw before reaching it. |
| `src/drive-loop.js#selectNextTicket` / `goalStuck` returning `null` | **CLEARED — and fail-safe in the OPPOSITE direction.** A legitimate empty selection returns null which `goalStuck` (`:174-177`) converts into a surface-to-human signal; the finder-broken case (`depsAreDone`, `:58-69`) THROWS naming the dangling key. Spot-checked independently. |
| `scripts/backfill-graph-task-nodes.mjs` / `migrate-graph-ids.mjs` zero-missing / zero-renamed | **CLEARED** — explicit console messages state the reason. |
| `src/close-guard.js` (`hasExplicitHumanVerdictMarker`, `uatComments.length === 0 -> false`) | **CLEARED** — fail-closed: empty denies rather than allows. |
| `src/task-store.js#checkUatGuard` feeding the uat-only close gate | **ESCALATED under AC6** — same class but on a close-guard path, out of scope for a `tests-after` ticket. Reworked under TASK-186. |
| `npm run test:changed` zero-selection on a clean/committed tree | **OUT OF FILE SCOPE — minted as TASK-194.** Same class, previously flagged 2026-07-06 as R23 and never actioned. |

## AC4 — the amendment, and why the evidence for it is now empirical
The developer had ALREADY implemented and empirically verified a hard-fail design (non-zero exit on zero selection) when my mid-flight amendment redirected it to a non-fatal self-describing marker. It reverted and rebuilt.

The reviewer then confirmed the amendment's premise by accident: running `test:since -- HEAD` against the real tree mid-review, on a tasks-bookkeeping-only diff, it organically produced `reason=no-spec-matched`. Under hard-fail that innocent run would have been a red gate. The alarm-fatigue argument is no longer speculative — it was observed.

The two markers: `reason=empty-diff` (committed + staged + unstaged all empty; legitimate, nothing to investigate) and `reason=no-spec-matched` (diff non-empty but `vitest list` matched zero specs — a docs-only, config-only, or fs-read-only change legitimately produces this). Either way the real `vitest run` still executes and its exit code passes through unchanged; **proven empirically — a genuine failing spec still exits 1 with output intact.** The wrapper cannot swallow failures.

## Measured cost (recorded per the reviewer's request)
The `vitest list` pre-check adds **5.2s** to every `test:since` run with a non-empty diff — roughly 20-30% overhead on a typical 15-30s gate run. The empty-diff branch adds only three sub-second git calls. Judged acceptable for de-ambiguating the reviewer gate itself, but it is a real recurring cost; re-weigh if the collect phase grows.

## Evidence quality
Both mutations re-run by the reviewer in scratchpad copies, both killed for the right reasons: planting `return false` in `hasAnyChangedFiles` flips the committed-diff and git-error cases; killing the detection branch flips the marker from `no-spec-matched` to `empty-diff`, failing both the `toMatch` and the `not.toMatch` assertions. Sensors are real. Mirror fidelity verified verbatim against vitest 2.1.9's `VitestGit` — identical three git commands, with one deliberate safe divergence (on git error the mirror conservatively reports "possibly changed" where vitest sees zero).

## Carried forward
**MEDIUM-2 — nothing pins `hasAnyChangedFiles` to vitest's algorithm across upgrades.** The comment cites a content-hash-named chunk (`git.B5SDxu-n.js`) that vanishes on the next vitest bump. Blast radius is bounded — a wrong reason LABEL, never a wrong exit code — but the label is this seam's whole deliverable. **Folded into TASK-194**, which will reuse this detection.

**LOW-1 — CLAUDE.md's "checkUatGuard is a presence-only check" was already stale at commit time**, six minutes after TASK-186's base commit upgraded it to a content check. The disposition ("being reworked under TASK-186") stays correct; only the characterization lags. One-line touch-up rides with TASK-186's close. This is the concurrent-siblings hazard in miniature — the same shape that made TASK-184 stale two minutes after it was fixed.

**LOW — a rejected extra arg can produce a false reason.** `extraArgs` are forwarded to `vitest list`; a run-only flag that `list` rejects yields a spurious `no-spec-matched` marker above a run that then selects specs normally. Marker-only and self-correcting on screen, but it is a wrong reason from the tool whose job is right reasons. Cheap hardening: treat a non-zero `listCheck.status` as "unknown" and say so.

## Gate
`npm test` 79 files / 1069 passed, 2 skipped · `test:since -- 1cf6fa6` 4 files / 30 passed (non-zero selection) · named e2e 5/5 · `npm run test:all` 174 files / 2004 passed, 4 skipped, exit 0, dist-parity green · `check:calibration` clean. TASK-081's pre-existing locks survive byte-intact — the diff is purely additive.
